title: What Registered Dietitians Do
description: Registered dietitian nutritionists translate nutrition science into eating: assessing nutritional status, diagnosing nutrition problems, designing medical nutrition therapy for diabetes, kidney, and heart disease, counseling on weight and wellness, and managing foodservice. They work in hospitals, clinics, schools, sports, and private practice.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in dietetics or related field (master's required from 2024)
Accredited supervised practice (dietetic internship)
RD exam via CDR; state licensure where required
Continuing professional education for renewal
standards: Evidence-based nutrition recommendations
Nutrition Care Process: assessment, diagnosis, intervention, monitoring
Culturally responsive counseling
Scope: RDNs are the nutrition experts; others may not use the title
safety: Screen for eating disorders and refer appropriately
Consider drug-nutrient interactions
Allergen awareness in all meal planning
Avoid one-size-fits-all restrictive advice

description: Continuous glucose monitors, AI meal analysis, telehealth counseling, and personalized nutrition from microbiome data are reshaping dietetics. RDNs who master the data lead — but the core stays human: counseling, culture, and the relationship that changes eating.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in dietetics or related field (master's required from 2024)
Accredited supervised practice (dietetic internship)
RD exam via CDR; state licensure where required
Continuing professional education for renewal
standards: Evidence-based nutrition recommendations
Nutrition Care Process: assessment, diagnosis, intervention, monitoring
Culturally responsive counseling
Scope: RDNs are the nutrition experts; others may not use the title
safety: Screen for eating disorders and refer appropriately
Consider drug-nutrient interactions
Allergen awareness in all meal planning
Avoid one-size-fits-all restrictive advice
troubleshooting: Client not following plan: simplify and re-motivate
Conflicting internet advice: return to evidence
Medical complexity: coordinate with the care team
Weight-loss plateau: reassess intake honestly
citations: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics guidance; Commission on Dietetic Registration standards; nutrition science references.
provenance: Public trade knowledge drawn from dietetics education, professional association guidance, and nutrition science references. Real, fact-checked records.
